system.name: M87*
system.description: The supermassive black hole at the heart of galaxy M87, 53.5 million light-years away. In April 2019 it became the first black hole ever directly imaged, its glowing accretion disk revealing a dark shadow the size of our entire solar system.

m87bh.name: M87*
m87bh.description: At 6.5 billion solar masses, M87* is one of the most massive black holes known. Its event horizon spans roughly 38 billion km — larger than our entire solar system. The Event Horizon Telescope image, assembled from radio dishes across Earth, showed the characteristic bright ring of superheated plasma encircling a dark shadow.
m87bh.funFact: M87* launches a relativistic jet of plasma stretching 5,000 light-years from its poles — one of the most powerful natural phenomena in the known universe.
